item.title: Osaka Tenmangu: Shrine of Scholars and the Tenjin Festival — Guide
item.description: Osaka Tenmangu enshrines Sugawara no Michizane, the ninth-century scholar-official deified as Tenjin, the god of learning, and it has drawn students praying for examination success for over a thousand years. Founded in 949, the shrine sits at the head of one of the longest shopping arcades in Japan and is the spiritual home of the Tenjin Matsuri, held each July — one of the three great festivals of Japan, in which sacred palanquins are carried to the river and paraded on a flotilla of boats beneath fireworks.

item.title: Tenjin Matsuri Guide: Osaka's Great River & Fire Festival
item.description: Held every July, Tenjin Matsuri is one of Japan’s three great festivals (with Kyoto’s Gion Matsuri and Tokyo’s Kanda Matsuri) and the biggest party in Osaka. Over a thousand years old, it honours Sugawara no Michizane, the deity of learning, enshrined at Osaka Tenmangu. The festival builds to a spectacular evening climax on July 25: a grand boat procession (funa-togyo) of around a hundred lantern-lit vessels gliding up and down the Okawa River, accompanied by drums, traditional music, and a fireworks finale reflected in the water.

item.title: Osaka Events 2026: Festivals, Fireworks, Sumo & USJ Happenings
item.description: Osaka does festivals the way it does everything — loud, warm, and food-first. The city’s 2026 calendar runs from one of Japan’s three great festivals (Tenjin Matsuri, with its river-boat procession and fireworks) to the heart-stopping cart races of Kishiwada Danjiri, a spring Grand Sumo tournament, the year’s biggest anime collaborations at Universal Studios Japan, and a cherry-blossom tunnel opened for just one week. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.
